One ought to seek out virtue for its own sake, without being influenced by fear or hope, or by any external influence. Moreover, that in that does happiness consist.

-Zeno of Citium (via Diogenes Laertius)

This begs the question, what is virtue? The word virtue comes from the Latin word virtus which means manliness, courage, virility, goodness, character. The root word for virtus is vir, which is literally "man". Zeno was clearly a Greek and not Roman, but when diving into these quotes it is sometimes necessary to look into the definition and history of words. Since virtue is in indelibly linked to men, we should ponder masculinity.

What is masculinity? And why should we seek it and virtue out for their own sake? I have my reasons, I want to hear yours.

On the idea that we should seek these things out for their own sake, to me that sounds like integrity. Do the right things for the right reasons, even when nobody is watching. Hell, especially when nobody is watching.

What is masculinity? And why should we seek it and virtue out for their own sake?

I like Robert Moore's analysis of the archetypes of masculinity as defined within the informative and highly accessible work King, Warrior, Magician, Lover: Rediscovering the Archetypes of the Mature Masculine . It's like an owner's manual for the male psyche.

Over the years, I've given many copies to friends who were mid-way through an evolution and having a rough go of it. If you haven't read it already, I recommend checking it out.

As to the 'why', that's easy: to be the highest and best version of me that I can be; a living manifestation of love. A devoted husband and father, a kind and benevolent leader, a powerful practitioner of the arcane arts and, if need be, a courageous warrior.

Do I always hit the mark? No. Which of us truly can?

It took my wife and children to open my heart to the world and stop living for myself. Once that happened, there was no turning back.

Do the right things for the right reasons, even when nobody is watching. Hell, especially when nobody is watching.

I realized a long time ago that there are no secrets. Anything that you have ever done, anything that you have ever said, hell - anything you have ever thought can be known to those who know how to seek it. I live my entire life that way, knowing that it's an open book.

Even if that weren't so, Seneca's advice to live as though someone who you respect is watching is sound.

Honesty in small things is not a small thing. Neither is integrity in every action one takes. Awesomeness is its own reward.

Summarily: You're not hardcore, unless you live hardcore
